standard_prerequisites: Chapter Lemma lemma-make-pre-equivalence (navigation stub, not delivered): replacing a pre-relation R by the pre-equivalence relation R-infinity it generates leaves weak orbits, orbits, and invariant morphisms unchanged, so orbit statements may be proven for pre-equivalence relations

Chapter Lemma lemma-weak-orbit-pre-equivalence (navigation stub, not delivered): for a pre-equivalence relation, R-equivalence of k-valued points over extension fields is expressed by the image of R(k) in U(k) times U(k)
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-permanence-finite-type: local finite type is preserved under composition
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite-type: local finite type is preserved under base change

Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-locally-finite-type-surjective-geometric-points: a nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over an algebraically closed field has a k-valued point
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-large-enough: the same conclusion holds over any algebraically closed field whose cardinality exceeds the bound lambda associated to the morphism
core_obligations: Part (1): assume s and t locally of finite type; by the make-pre-equivalence lemma reduce to the case where R is a pre-equivalence relation; given u-bar and u-bar-prime in U(k) that are R-equivalent, the weak-orbit lemma provides a field extension and a point r-bar of R over the pair; hence the fibre product Z of R over j with Spec of k at that pair is nonempty

Since s is locally of finite type, j is locally of finite type by the permanence lemma, and Z is then a nonempty algebraic space locally of finite type over the algebraically closed field k by the base-change lemma

By the geometric-point lemma Z has a k-valued point, which is a k-valued point r-bar of R with j(r-bar) equal to the pair; hence u-bar and u-bar-prime are R-equivalent as k-valued points, proving weak equivalence agrees with equivalence and likewise for orbits
Part (2): the proof is the same with the geometric-point lemma replaced by the large-enough lemma, which shows the agreement holds as soon as the cardinality of k exceeds lambda(R)
proof_roadmap: Reduce to pre-equivalence relations and produce the nonempty fibre product from an R-equivalence over an extension field
Extract a k-valued point of the locally finite type fibre product over the algebraically closed field
Re-run the same chain under the large cardinality hypothesis for part (2)
